chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Often a poor person is more extravagant than the rich one. Indeed, the rich one spends from what he has been given, and the poor one spends from that which does not belong to him.

key_terms.غَيْرِ مَا أُوتِيَ: that which was not given to him (not his own wealth)
key_terms.مِمَّا أُوتِيَ: from what he has been given (his own wealth)

ai.seo_question: Why is a poor person sometimes more extravagant than a rich person?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi offers a nuanced critique of *israf* (extravagance) by contrasting the poor, who may spend from what they have not earned or do not own, with the rich, who spend from their legitimate wealth. It underscores the ethical principle that the source and nature of the funds matter more than the amount, warning against the spiritual and financial ruin caused by the poor incurring debt or misappropriating resources to maintain appearances.
